messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: 5xx rate > 4x baseline for /v1/generate in prod-us-west (p95 latency ↑ 6x). Deploy tagged "deploy/2026-03-17-21:10" rolled ~21:10 UTC. Pager sent to #incidents.
ben-oncall: I'm on it. seeing elevated 502/504 from api-gateway; starting triage. who deployed? :eyes:
carla-frontend: that deploy was the routing-change PR (mux + keepalive tweaks) — build 2026-03-17-21:09, canary passed but rollout hit 50% at 21:09.
dan-sre: grabbing logs from gateway and runtime. hitting `kubectl logs gateway -n prod --since=30m | grep generate | head` now.
frank-eng: flagged the PR owner (sam) and dropping into the canary matrix. putting a block on further rollouts.
ben-oncall: telemetry: p95 went from 120ms -> 1.1s, p99 -> 4.8s. 5xx dominated by upstream timeouts to runtime pool (connection reset / timeout).
eva-support: support queue picking up errors from a handful of high-traffic customers (chatbots) — some are seeing repeated timeouts.
dan-sre: gateway logs snippet:
```
2026-03-17T21:12:03Z gateway[proxy] ERROR downstream=client upstream=runtime-12:504 message="upstream request timeout"
2026-03-17T21:12:04Z gateway[proxy] WARN conn=keepalive recycle_failed: EOF
```
carla-frontend: config change in PR: increased mux multiplexing window + disabled aggressive keepalive recycle for idle conns. hypothesis: multiplexing + longer-lived sessions causing connection saturation on certain runtime pods.
ben-oncall: can we reduce traffic to the new revision (roll back the routing change) or route around region? prefer rollback of routing change to previous stable.
dan-sre: two mitigations we can do in parallel:
- roll traffic back to stable version (route shift at gateway) — fast
- scale up runtime pool / drain bad pods — slower
I'm starting the route-shift now: `kubectl patch svc/gateway -n prod -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"version":"stable"}}}'` (will do via orchestration pipeline).
frank-eng: quick test: `curl -v https://api.prod/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer x'` against stable shows normal latencies ~140ms.
carla-frontend: confirm: pushing route-shift to 10% -> 0% for new revision. doing canary rollback in traffic-manager.
eva-support: please post a short customer-impact blurb once we know scope so we can update support threads.
ben-oncall: route shift applied. monitoring.
incident-bot: Notation: mitigation action ROUTE_SHIFT executed by ben-oncall at 3599999994.
dan-sre: meters:
- 5xx-rate down from 4x -> 1.3x in 120s
- p95 down from 1.1s -> 180ms in 240s
Looks promising.
frank-eng: also observed many keepalive-reset logs on runtime-12/14/15; draining runtime-12 now: `kubectl cordon runtime-12 && kubectl drain runtime-12 --ignore-daemonsets`.
carla-frontend: note: the change also touched connection pooling config — planning followup PR to revert mux window changes and add more conservative keepalive backoff.
eva-support: initial impact summary for support:
- ~7 customers reported timeouts between 21:11-21:20 UTC
- transient; most recovered after 21:15 following route-shift
- no data loss, retries succeeded
I'll post templated update to affected customers and the support ticket.
ben-oncall: handoff: I'm going to remain on-call for 10m to confirm stability, then hand to dan-sre for postmortem and followup fixes. dan, pls pick up after 21:25 UTC.
dan-sre: ack, will own followups and coordinate rollback PR + runbook updates. please attach metrics dashboards and sample logs to the incident.
frank-eng: quick note for postmortem: add hypothesis test to reproduce multiplexing under high-concurrency small payloads. include load test for keepalive behavior.
incident-bot: INCIDENT: resolved -> symptom reduced below threshold. closed by ben-oncall at 3600000030. duration ~1m31s.
ben-oncall: closing notes: rolled routing back to stable, drained 3 runtime pods showing keepalive EOF errors, no rollback of code required (config routing change only). prepping a short incident report. :white_check_mark:
eva-support: updating support tickets and CC'ing affected customers.
dan-sre: will open a postmortem ticket and link to this thread. assigning remediation to carla-frontend (revert mux window) and frank-eng (stress test).
